facts.statement: The genus Archaeotriakis was described by Case in 1978.
The genus includes two species: Archaeotriakis rochelleae and Archaeotriakis ornatus.
Archaeotriakis was an extinct false catshark that lived during the Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Archaeotriakis is an extinct genus of false catshark from the Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The genus is currently known only from the Campanian stage of the Western Interior Seaway in North America.
facts.quote: Currently, this genus is restricted to the Campanian stage of the Western Interior Seaway of North America.

facts.statement: Fossils of Archaeotriakis are known mainly from isolated teeth.
facts.quote: It is known from two species, mainly from isolated teeth.

facts.statement: Archaeotriakis rochelleae was described from fossils found in the Judith River Formation of Montana, USA.
facts.quote: A. rochelleae was described from the Judith River Formation of Montana, USA.

facts.statement: Archaeotriakis ornatus was originally described from the Teapot Member of the Mesaverde Group in Wyoming, USA.
facts.quote: A. ornatus was originally described from the Teapot Member of the Mesaverde Group of Wyoming, USA.

facts.statement: The range of Archaeotriakis ornatus has also been found in the Bearpaw Formation of Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: The range of A. ornatus has since been found in the Bearpaw formation of Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: Archaeotriakis belongs to the family Triakidae.
Archaeotriakis is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Archaeotriakis lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
